item: A newsletter removal that fails partway says how many articles are removed and how many are left, and the salvage's epoch bump is strict (queue item 58)
summary: Queue item 58, two follow-ups from PR #1865 (the coordinator, 2026-11-09 03:51Z). BEFORE: (a) delete_imported_newsletters removes in chunks of 900, each committed with a strict corpus-epoch bump; a chunk that failed (one of its deletes, or its bump) escaped as whatever the failure was, so POST /api/newsletters/remove-imported answered a bare 500 while the earlier chunks were already removed and Keyword.mention_count/article_count and the per-source counters still counted them (the counter repair ran only after the last chunk), and the settings panel kept the count it had before. (b) repair._after_the_swap bumped the epoch non-strictly, so a failure was swallowed inside bump_corpus_epoch, which handed back the epoch the damaged file already had, and the repair report's corpus_epoch read as if bumped. NOW: (a) a failed chunk is rolled back whole, the counters are refreshed for the chunks already removed (only when one was), and NewsletterRemovalStopped (a RuntimeError, raised outside the handler so the failure is not chained to it) carries removed, total and counts_refreshed; the failure is logged scrubbed where it happened. The route answers 500 in those fixed words, through http_detail, e.g. 'The removal stopped after removing 4 of the 5 imported newsletter articles; the other 1 is still in your corpus. Run the removal again to remove it.', plus 'Until then, some keyword and source counts may read high.' when the refresh also failed, or 'The removal stopped before it removed any of the N ...' for a first-chunk failure. Counters that cannot be refreshed after a complete removal no longer turn it into a 500: the 200 carries counts_refreshed false and a note in fixed words, which the panel shows as text. The panel refreshes the remaining count after a stopped removal too. (b) the bump is strict=True: a failure reads None and the log says 'the corpus epoch was not bumped (<type>); the keyword rollup may count rows the repair could not keep until the next epoch bump' (the type only, as the repair logs). The per-day keyword counts need nothing more: Salvage._finish already marks them unbuilt in the copy (pinned in tests/test_day_counts.py). TESTS: tests/test_partial_removal_and_salvage_epoch_item58.py, 11, through the real removal, the real write gate and the real route (TestClient over a file-backed store; only the failures are planted, a planted needle never reaches the answer): 10 fail on 787366d50, the control (a working salvage bump reads the new epoch) passes. 16 mutants (the salvage bump non-strict, no rollback of a failed chunk, the refresh run when nothing was removed, the raise inside the handler, the chunk counted before it commits, the words' counts clause, singular and plural, the counts swapped, the success note and flag, the refresh helper claiming success, the route without its catch, the panel's count refresh and its note as markup, the repair log without the lag, a first-chunk failure worded as a removal): all killed. NOT CHANGED: a removal that stops because the process ends (not a failure) leaves the counters stale until it runs again, as stated in its docstring; the counter deferral marker (R22) is not opened by a removal, so the counters keep reporting exact until refreshed; after a failed salvage bump the columnar rollup keeps counting what the repair lost until the next epoch bump (stated in the log, not retried). Release-notes line: «Removing imported newsletters no longer ends in an internal error when it fails partway: it says how many were removed and how many are left, and running it again removes the rest. After the app repairs a damaged library file, its repair record and log now say when the keyword caches were not told to rebuild, instead of reading as if they were.»
